title: Checkpoint: Top-K frequent words
prompt: Implement `std::vector<std::string> top_k(const std::vector<std::string>& words, std::size_t k)` returning the k most frequent words ordered by count descending; ties are broken lexicographically (smaller word first). If there are fewer than k distinct words, return all of them (still ordered). Combine a counting `std::map` with a sort (or a `std::priority_queue`) — the tie-break rule is the part most solutions get wrong.
